Architect.summary: Design buildings and spaces by combining creativity, math, technology, codes and collaboration.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Geometry, Algebra II/Precalculus, Physics, art/design, drafting/CAD and strong writing/presentation skills.
College / Architecture Curriculum
Typical architecture coursework: design studio, architectural history, structures, building systems, environmental systems, CAD/BIM and professional practice.
Experience
Build a design portfolio and complete architecture/design internships or approved professional experience.
Credentials / Qualifications
Follow the professional degree + experience + licensing-exam route required where you plan to practice.
Career Launch
Begin in an architecture/design firm, develop a specialty and work toward independent licensure.
Architect.scene: a modern architectural studio with drawings, scale models, blueprints, and a contemporary building visible through windows

Electrician.summary: Install, troubleshoot and maintain electrical systems in homes, businesses, industry and new construction.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Algebra, Physics, electronics, measurement, technical/shop courses, blueprint reading and safety.
Apprenticeship / Technical Curriculum
Typical apprenticeship coursework: electrical theory, National Electrical Code, wiring methods, blueprint reading, motors/controls, troubleshooting and jobsite safety.
Experience
Complete paid supervised on-the-job apprenticeship hours while progressing through classroom instruction.
Credentials / Qualifications
Meet state requirements for the appropriate electrical credential or license; exact rules vary by state.
Career Launch
Work in residential, commercial or industrial electrical systems; later move into estimating, supervision or business ownership.
Electrician.scene: a clean commercial electrical work site, wearing appropriate professional electrician work clothing and safety equipment, with tools and electrical panels in the background

Registered Nurse.summary: Provide direct patient care, coordinate treatment, and educate patients and families.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Biology, Chemistry, Anatomy & Physiology, Algebra/Statistics, Health and strong English communication.
College / Nursing Curriculum

Typical ADN/BSN coursework: anatomy & physiology, microbiology, pharmacology, pathophysiology, nursing fundamentals, medical-surgical nursing, pediatrics, maternity, mental health and community health.
Experience
Complete supervised clinical rotations in hospitals, clinics and other approved healthcare settings.
Credentials / Qualifications
Graduate from an approved nursing program, pass the NCLEX-RN and meet state licensure requirements.
Career Launch
Begin as an RN, then develop a specialty in hospital, clinic, school, community or other nursing settings.
Registered Nurse.scene: a bright modern hospital or medical center, wearing professional nursing scrubs with no visible logos, in a realistic clinical environment

Veterinarian.summary: Diagnose and treat animals while advising owners about health, prevention and care.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Biology, Chemistry, Physics, math and animal-care or science experiences.
College + Veterinary School Curriculum

College prerequisites commonly include biology, chemistry, organic chemistry, physics and math. DVM study includes anatomy, physiology, microbiology, pathology, pharmacology, diagnostics, surgery and clinical rotations.
Experience
Accumulate documented animal/veterinary experience and complete supervised clinical rotations in veterinary school.
Credentials / Qualifications
Earn a DVM and satisfy national/state veterinary licensing requirements.
Career Launch
Work in companion-animal, large-animal, specialty, public-health, research or mixed practice.
Veterinarian.scene: a welcoming modern veterinary clinic, wearing professional veterinary clothing, with a friendly dog nearby and medical equipment subtly in the background

Software Developer.summary: Design and build software, websites, apps and digital systems.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Algebra II, Computer Science, Web Development, Statistics, technology courses and strong problem solving.
College / Software Curriculum
Typical coursework: programming, object-oriented design, data structures, algorithms, databases, operating systems, networks, software engineering, web/mobile development and cloud fundamentals.
Experience
Build a portfolio of working projects, use version control, and pursue internships, hackathons or open-source work.
Credentials / Qualifications
A degree can help, but strong portfolios, internships and validated technical skills also matter; no universal license is required.
Career Launch
Apply for junior developer, QA/automation, web or software-engineering roles and keep expanding your project portfolio.
Software Developer.scene: a modern software development workspace with code on monitors, collaborative technology office setting, professional casual clothing

Teacher.summary: Help students learn, think, communicate and grow in a general education classroom.
steps: High School Curriculum
Build strong English communication plus depth in the subject or age group you may want to teach; add psychology/human-behavior, public-speaking and tutoring/mentoring experiences where possible.
College / Educator-Preparation Curriculum

Typical educator-preparation coursework: foundations of education, child/adolescent development, educational psychology, instructional methods, classroom management, assessment, inclusive education and subject-area teaching methods.
Experience
Complete classroom observations, field experiences and a supervised student-teaching placement.
Credentials / Qualifications
Earn the required degree/approved educator-preparation credential and meet state certification requirements for your grade/subject area.
Career Launch
Apply to schools/districts, complete induction/mentoring requirements and continue professional learning.
Teacher.scene: a bright contemporary general education high school classroom, standing near student desks and a whiteboard, dressed as a professional educator, with students engaged in a class lesson

Special Education Teacher.summary: Help students with disabilities learn, build independence and reach individualized academic, social and transition goals.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize English communication, psychology/human behavior, strong subject foundations and supervised peer-support or adaptive-program experiences.
College / Special-Education Curriculum

Typical coursework: exceptional learners, IEP development, assessment, behavior supports, assistive technology, literacy/numeracy interventions, inclusive instruction, collaboration and special-education law/ethics.
Experience
Complete supervised field placements and student teaching with students who have varied learning and support needs.
Credentials / Qualifications
Complete an approved special-education teacher-preparation program and meet state certification/endorsement requirements.
Career Launch
Begin in resource, inclusion, life-skills or other special-education settings and continue specialty training.
Special Education Teacher.scene: a bright contemporary special education classroom in a high school, dressed as a professional educator, supporting a small group of students with accessible learning materials and assistive technology visible in a respectful inclusive setting

Firefighter.summary: Respond to fires, medical emergencies, rescues and community safety needs.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Health, Biology/Chemistry, PE/fitness, technical courses, English communication and service/leadership.
Fire Academy / EMS Curriculum
Typical academy topics: fire behavior, suppression, ladders, search/rescue, building construction, hazardous materials, incident command, equipment operation and emergency medical response.
Experience
Seek approved cadet/volunteer/community-service exposure where available and maintain strong physical conditioning.
Credentials / Qualifications
Departments commonly require academy certification and often EMT credentials; exact hiring standards vary by department/state.
Career Launch
Compete for municipal or regional firefighter positions, then add specialty/rescue/EMS certifications over time.
Firefighter.scene: outside a modern fire station beside a fire engine, wearing clean professional firefighter turnout gear with helmet held at the side, no active emergency or flames

Police Officer.summary: Protect the community, respond to emergencies, investigate incidents and work with residents.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Civics, Law, English, Psychology/Human Behavior, Forensic Science and physical fitness.
College / Police-Academy Curriculum

Relevant college study may include criminal justice, psychology, sociology, writing and law. Police academy training typically covers criminal law/procedure, report writing, de-escalation, emergency driving, defensive tactics and community policing.
Experience
Build a record of service, communication and responsibility; explore approved public-safety internships/cadet opportunities where available.
Credentials / Qualifications
Meet department hiring standards and complete the required state/agency police academy and certification process.
Career Launch
Begin patrol training, then pursue specialties such as investigations, community policing, school resource, traffic or leadership.
Police Officer.scene: a professional community-policing setting outside a civic building, wearing a generic police uniform with no real department insignia, calm non-confrontational scene

TV News Reporter / Local Anchor.summary: Research, report and explain news stories clearly on camera and across digital platforms.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize English, journalism-style writing, Digital Cinematography, Civics/current events, media literacy and public speaking.
College / Journalism Curriculum

Typical journalism/broadcast coursework: reporting and news writing, media law/ethics, broadcast production, digital storytelling, video editing, interviewing, public-affairs reporting and investigative methods.
Experience
Create a reel/portfolio, report on real school/community stories and pursue newsroom, station or digital-media internships.
Credentials / Qualifications
No universal license; employers look closely at reporting skill, writing, on-camera performance, ethics and a strong demo reel.
Career Launch
Start in local/digital reporting, producing or multimedia journalism and build toward anchoring or specialty beats.

Broadway Director / Actor.summary: Build a professional life in theatre through acting, directing, auditions, rehearsal and production experience.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Theatre, Script Analysis, English, music/dance when relevant, technical theatre and frequent live-performance experience.
College / Theatre Curriculum
Typical theatre coursework: acting, voice/speech, movement, directing, script analysis, theatre history, stagecraft/design, audition technique and production practicum.
Experience
Perform, direct or crew as many productions as possible; build an audition portfolio and relationships with working theatre artists.
Credentials / Qualifications
A degree is common but not mandatory; professional success depends heavily on auditions, credits, training, portfolio and network.
Career Launch
Pursue regional/community/professional productions, assistant-directing, workshops and auditions while building credits.
Broadway Director / Actor.scene: inside a beautiful professional Broadway-style theatre during rehearsal, stage lights glowing, dressed in stylish theatre-professional clothing, with stage and empty seats visible

Chef / Restaurant Owner.summary: Create food, lead kitchen teams and potentially build a restaurant or food business.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize math, business, accounting, marketing, Health, nutrition/food-safety learning and part-time food-service experience.
Culinary / Hospitality Curriculum

Typical culinary or hospitality study: culinary fundamentals, sanitation/food safety, baking, nutrition, menu planning, food cost control, purchasing, hospitality operations, accounting and entrepreneurship.
Experience
Work in real kitchens/restaurants, learn multiple stations and observe both front-of-house and back-of-house operations.
Credentials / Qualifications
Food-safety credentials may be required; culinary degrees/certificates are optional but can accelerate skill development.
Career Launch
Begin in kitchen/restaurant operations, advance to supervisory roles, then develop a business plan before ownership.

Automotive Technician.summary: Diagnose, repair and maintain cars and light trucks using mechanical and computerized systems.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Algebra, Physics, Electronics, Automotive/technology courses, computer diagnostics and safe tool use.
Automotive-Technology Curriculum
Typical training: engine systems, brakes, steering/suspension, electrical/electronic systems, HVAC, drivability, scan-tool diagnostics and shop safety.
Experience
Complete hands-on lab/shop work and pursue dealership, independent-shop or fleet internships/apprenticeships.
Credentials / Qualifications
ASE certifications are widely valued; manufacturer-specific training can add specialized credentials.
Career Launch
Start as an entry-level/lube or apprentice technician and progress into diagnostic specialties, master technician or shop leadership.

Physical Therapist.summary: Help people restore movement, strength and function after injury or illness.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Biology, Chemistry, Anatomy & Physiology, Physics, Statistics and health/fitness science.
College + DPT Curriculum

Pre-PT study commonly includes biology, chemistry, physics, anatomy/physiology and statistics. DPT coursework includes kinesiology, neuroscience, biomechanics, pathology, therapeutic exercise, examination/intervention and clinical practice.
Experience
Gain observation hours where programs require/recommend them and complete full-time clinical rotations during DPT training.
Credentials / Qualifications
Earn a Doctor of Physical Therapy degree, pass the NPTE and meet state licensure requirements.
Career Launch
Begin in outpatient, hospital, rehab, sports, pediatric, school or other PT settings and later specialize if desired.

Plumber.summary: Install, repair and maintain water, drainage and piping systems in homes, businesses and construction projects.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Algebra/Geometry, Physics, drafting, construction/shop courses, measurement and jobsite safety.
Apprenticeship / Plumbing Curriculum
Typical apprenticeship topics: pipefitting, water supply, drainage/waste/vent systems, gas systems, plumbing code, blueprint reading, applied math and safety.
Experience
Complete paid supervised apprenticeship hours on residential/commercial jobs while completing classroom instruction.
Credentials / Qualifications
Meet state/local requirements for apprentice, journeyperson and/or contractor licensing as applicable.
Career Launch
Work in service, construction or industrial plumbing; later move into estimating, supervision or business ownership.

Business Administration / Manager.summary: Plan, organize and lead people, budgets and operations so an organization can reach its goals.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize English, Algebra/Statistics, Business, Accounting, Economics, Marketing and leadership experiences.
College / Business Curriculum
Typical business coursework: management, accounting, finance, marketing, economics, operations, human resources, business law, analytics and organizational behavior.
Experience
Use internships, school leadership, part-time work and project management to practice supervising people and solving operational problems.
Credentials / Qualifications
A bachelor’s degree is common for many management-track roles; specific industries may value additional certifications.
Career Launch
Begin in operations, sales, finance, HR or management-training roles and build toward team/department leadership.

Carpenter.summary: Build, install and repair structures and finishes using wood and other construction materials.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Geometry, measurement, drafting, woodworking, construction technology and jobsite safety.
Apprenticeship / Carpentry Curriculum
Typical training: blueprint reading, framing, finish carpentry, materials, layout/measurement, estimating, tool operation and OSHA/jobsite safety.
Experience
Build hands-on experience through shop classes, construction projects and paid apprenticeship or contractor employment.
Credentials / Qualifications
Formal apprenticeship is valuable; contractor licensing/certification requirements depend on location and scope of work.

Work in residential/commercial carpentry, then specialize in framing, finish work, cabinetry, renovation or supervision.

Graphic Designer.summary: Create visual communications for print, digital media, brands, campaigns, products and organizations.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Foundations in Design, Digital Imaging, Graphic Media, photography/art and strong writing/communication.
College / Design Curriculum
Typical design coursework: design principles, typography, color theory, branding, illustration, digital imaging, layout, UX basics, portfolio development and professional practice.
Experience
Build a strong portfolio from real projects, school/community clients, internships and personal design work.
Credentials / Qualifications
No universal license; portfolio quality and software/design skill are usually more important than certifications alone.

Apply for junior graphic, brand, production or digital-design roles and continue building a specialized portfolio.

Neurosurgeon.summary: Diagnose and surgically treat complex conditions affecting the brain, spine and nervous system.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize advanced Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Calculus/Statistics, Anatomy & Physiology and strong reading/writing.
College + Medical-School Curriculum

Pre-med coursework typically includes biology, general/organic chemistry, biochemistry, physics, calculus/statistics and psychology/sociology. Medical school adds anatomy, neuroanatomy, physiology, pathology, pharmacology and clinical rotations.
Experience
Build healthcare/research exposure, then complete medical-school clinical rotations followed by a highly intensive neurosurgery residency.
Credentials / Qualifications
Earn an MD/DO, pass medical licensing exams, complete neurosurgery residency and meet board/state requirements.
Career Launch
Practice as a hospital/academic/private neurosurgeon, often with further subspecialty fellowship training.

Cybersecurity Specialist.summary: Protect computers, networks and information from attacks, misuse and security failures.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Computer Science, networking/electronics, Algebra, Web Development and hands-on system troubleshooting.
College / Cybersecurity Curriculum
Typical coursework: networking, Linux, programming, security fundamentals, cryptography, digital forensics, cloud security, ethical hacking, incident response and risk management.
Experience
Build labs/home projects, compete in cyber challenges and pursue IT/help-desk/security internships.
Credentials / Qualifications
Industry certifications such as Security+, Network+ or vendor/cloud credentials can complement a degree and experience.
Career Launch
Start in IT support, SOC/security analyst, network/security or junior cyber roles and specialize over time.

Data Scientist / AI Specialist.summary: Use statistics, programming and machine learning to find patterns in data and build useful predictive or AI systems.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Algebra II, Precalculus/Calculus, Statistics, Computer Science/Python and strong analytical writing.
College / Data-AI Curriculum
Typical coursework: calculus, linear algebra, probability/statistics, programming, data structures, databases, machine learning, AI, data visualization and experimental methods.
Experience
Build data projects, model portfolios and internships using real datasets; learn to explain results clearly to nontechnical audiences.
Credentials / Qualifications
Bachelor’s degrees are common; advanced AI/research roles may prefer graduate study. No universal professional license.
Career Launch
Start in data analyst, junior data scientist, ML/AI engineering or analytics roles and deepen a technical specialty.

Prioritize Biology, Chemistry, Anatomy & Physiology, Health and strong interpersonal communication.
Dental-Hygiene Curriculum
Typical accredited-program coursework: oral anatomy, radiography, periodontology, dental materials, pharmacology, preventive dentistry, community dental health and supervised clinical practice.
Experience
Complete extensive supervised dental-hygiene clinical hours with real patients in an accredited program.
Credentials / Qualifications
Graduate from an accredited dental-hygiene program and meet national/state examination and licensure requirements.

Work in dental practices, public health, education or specialty settings and add expanded-function credentials where available.

Prioritize Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Calculus/Statistics, Anatomy & Physiology and strong English communication.
College + Medical-School Curriculum

Pre-med coursework commonly includes biology, general/organic chemistry, biochemistry, physics, calculus/statistics and psychology/sociology. Medical school includes anatomy, physiology, pathology, pharmacology, diagnostics and clinical rotations.
Experience
Build healthcare/service/research exposure, then complete clinical rotations and residency in a medical specialty.
Credentials / Qualifications
Earn an MD/DO, pass required licensing exams, complete residency and meet state/board requirements.

Practice in a chosen specialty after residency; some physicians add fellowship subspecialty training.

HVAC Technician.summary: Install, maintain and repair heating, ventilation, air-conditioning and refrigeration systems.

Prioritize Algebra, Physics, Electronics & Engineering, measurement, technical/shop courses and safety.
HVAC Technical Curriculum
Typical training: refrigeration cycles, electrical controls, heating/cooling systems, airflow, blueprint reading, diagnostics, EPA refrigerant rules and jobsite safety.
Experience
Complete hands-on lab work and employer/apprenticeship experience troubleshooting real HVAC systems.

EPA Section 608 certification is commonly required for refrigerant work; state/local trade licenses vary.

Begin as an HVAC installer/service apprentice and progress into diagnostics, controls, commercial systems or supervision.

Lawyer / Attorney.summary: Advise clients, interpret laws, research issues and advocate in negotiations, transactions or court proceedings.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize English, History/Civics, Law, debate/public speaking, Economics and research-heavy writing.
College + Law-School Curriculum

College can be any rigorous major emphasizing reading/writing/research. Typical first-year law courses include contracts, torts, civil procedure, criminal law, constitutional law, property and legal research/writing, followed by electives and clinics.
Experience
Build research, debate, service and internship experience; in law school use clinics, moot court and summer legal placements.
Credentials / Qualifications
Earn a JD from an approved law school and satisfy bar-admission requirements in the jurisdiction where you plan to practice.

Begin in a firm, government, nonprofit, corporate or public-interest legal role and develop a practice area.

Prioritize English, Marketing/Business, Digital Imaging/Graphic Media, Statistics and presentation skills.
College / Marketing Curriculum
Typical coursework: marketing principles, consumer behavior, market research, digital/social media, advertising, branding, sales, analytics and campaign strategy.
Experience
Create real campaigns, social/content projects and a portfolio; pursue internships with businesses, agencies or nonprofits.

A degree is common; platform/analytics certifications can strengthen a portfolio but no universal license exists.

Start in marketing coordination, content, social media, account service, sales or analytics and grow toward strategy/management.

College / Health-Administration Curriculum
Typical coursework: healthcare systems, health policy, healthcare finance/accounting, HR, operations, health informatics, quality improvement, statistics, law/ethics and management.
Experience
Seek healthcare-office, hospital, clinic or administrative internships and learn how patient-care organizations operate.

A bachelor’s degree is common; larger/senior roles may prefer graduate study such as MHA/MBA/MPH.

Build RN clinical experience and complete advanced supervised NP clinical hours in the chosen population specialty.

Earn required graduate nursing preparation, national NP certification and state APRN licensure/authority requirements.

College + OT Graduate Curriculum
Typical OT study: anatomy, neuroscience, kinesiology, psychosocial practice, activity analysis, pediatrics, adult rehabilitation, assistive technology, research and fieldwork.
Experience
Complete observation/volunteer experiences and extensive supervised fieldwork during an accredited OT program.

Earn an accredited OT graduate degree, pass the NBCOT exam and meet state licensure requirements.

Work in hospitals, rehab, schools, pediatrics, mental health, skilled nursing or community settings.

Prioritize Biology, Chemistry, Anatomy & Physiology, Statistics and strong communication.

Build the patient-care experience expected by target PA programs and complete intensive supervised clinical rotations.

Graduate from an accredited PA program, pass the PANCE and meet state licensure requirements.

Practice on a physician-led/collaborative healthcare team in primary care, surgery, emergency medicine or another specialty.

Prioritize Business, Accounting, Marketing, Economics, English, technology/web skills and real selling/project experience.
Business / Entrepreneurship Curriculum
Useful coursework: entrepreneurship, accounting, finance, marketing, operations, sales, business law, e-commerce, analytics and management.
Experience
Start a small real project: sell a product/service, track costs/revenue, test marketing, gather customer feedback and improve the model.
Credentials / Qualifications
No required degree or license for entrepreneurship itself, though the chosen industry may have permits, licenses or professional credentials.
Career Launch
Validate a problem/customer, build a lean business plan, manage cash flow and grow only after proving demand.
Entrepreneur / Business Owner.scene: a confident small-business owner in a contemporary office or storefront, professional attire, collaborating with a small team with generic business materials visible

Military / Armed Forces.summary: Serve in one of the U.S. Armed Forces in a military specialty that may involve leadership, technology, logistics, medicine, engineering, aviation, communications or other fields.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize English, math, science, physical fitness, technology, Civics and World Language when useful for your interests.
Service / Officer-Training Curriculum

Enlisted route: basic training plus a job-specific technical school. Officer routes may include college + ROTC, a service academy or Officer Candidate/Training School. Technical curriculum depends on specialty: aviation, cyber, logistics, medicine, intelligence, engineering and more.
Experience
Research branches and specialties carefully, compare service commitments/benefits and speak with family, counselors, veterans and official recruiters before deciding.
Credentials / Qualifications
Meet service eligibility, testing, medical/fitness and training requirements; some specialties also provide civilian-recognized technical credentials.
Career Launch
Enter an enlisted specialty or commissioning path and deliberately track civilian-transferable skills, education and certifications.
Military / Armed Forces.scene: a respectful modern military professional setting with generic U.S. service-style uniform and no readable insignia, weapons, combat scene, recruitment slogan or branch logo; confident service member in a technical or leadership environment

Customer Service Representative.summary: Help customers solve problems, understand products or services, and have a positive experience with a business or organization.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize English, Business, Marketing/Sales, computer applications, digital communication and part-time/service experience.
Workplace / Business Training

Common training topics: customer communication, de-escalation, product/service knowledge, CRM software, data entry, business writing, privacy/security and problem resolution. College is not always required.
Experience
Use retail, hospitality, office, school-help-desk or volunteer roles to practice solving problems for real people.
Credentials / Qualifications
No universal license; role-specific product, software or industry certifications may help.
Career Launch
Begin in customer service/support and progress into senior support, quality, training, sales, operations or supervision.
Customer Service Representative.scene: a modern customer support workplace with a friendly professional at a desk using a computer and headset, clean office setting, no readable customer data or company logos

Elected Official / Politician.summary: Represent a community in public office by listening to constituents, studying issues, building coalitions and helping shape laws, budgets and policy.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Civics, History, English, Economics, Law, debate/public speaking, Media Literacy and community involvement.
College / Public-Policy Curriculum

Common useful college study includes political science, public policy, economics, communications or law, with courses such as American government, constitutional law, public policy, statistics, economics and public speaking. A specific degree is not legally required for elected office.
Experience
Volunteer on campaigns/community boards, attend public meetings, organize around an issue and learn constituent communication.
Credentials / Qualifications
Eligibility rules depend on the office and jurisdiction; credibility comes from community involvement, knowledge, ethics and leadership.
Career Launch
Begin with community/campaign service, appointed boards or local office and build a public record before seeking larger roles.
Elected Official / Politician.scene: a professional civic setting such as a town hall or legislative chamber, dressed in business attire, speaking with community members or reviewing public-policy materials, no party logos or campaign signs

Caregiver / Personal Care Aide.summary: Support older adults or people with disabilities with daily living, safety, companionship and independence in homes or care settings.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Health, Anatomy/biology, psychology/human behavior, CPR/first aid and supervised peer-support/service experiences.
Direct-Care Training Curriculum

Typical training: personal care, infection control, mobility/transfers, nutrition, dementia/disability support, communication, documentation, emergency response and client rights. CNA/HHA training may be useful or required for certain roles/settings.
Experience
Build supervised experience helping people with daily participation, independence and social/emotional support.
Credentials / Qualifications
Requirements vary by job and setting; CPR/first aid and CNA/HHA or agency training may be required.
Career Launch
Work in home care, assisted living, disability support, senior care or community programs and build specialty credentials.
Caregiver / Personal Care Aide.scene: a warm professional home-care or senior-living setting, respectfully assisting an older adult with everyday activities, professional caregiver attire, no medical emergency imagery

Construction Manager.summary: Plan and coordinate construction projects by managing schedules, budgets, safety, contractors, materials, quality and communication.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Geometry/Algebra, drafting/CAD, engineering, woodworking/construction, Business and Accounting.
College / Construction-Management Curriculum
Typical coursework: construction methods/materials, estimating, scheduling, contracts, safety, blueprint reading/BIM, cost control, project management, accounting and field operations.
Experience
Pursue construction-site internships/co-ops and learn how superintendents, trades, designers, owners and inspectors coordinate.
Credentials / Qualifications
A bachelor’s degree is common for management-track roles; industry safety/project credentials can strengthen advancement.
Career Launch
Begin as project engineer/assistant PM/field coordinator and progress toward project manager or superintendent.
Construction Manager.scene: a professional construction site office and active building project, wearing appropriate hard hat and safety vest, reviewing plans with a project team, no company logos

Psychologist.summary: Study behavior and mental processes and, depending on specialty and licensure, assess, research or help people improve mental health and functioning.
steps: High School Curriculum
Prioritize Human Behavior/Psychology, Biology, Statistics, English/research writing and helping/research experiences.
College + Psychology Graduate Curriculum

Typical undergraduate psychology: developmental, abnormal, social, cognitive and biological psychology, research methods and statistics. Clinical/counseling graduate study adds assessment, psychotherapy, ethics, advanced research, practicum and internship.
Experience
Build research/helping experience; clinical psychologists complete extensive supervised practicum/internship training.
Credentials / Qualifications
Independent clinical psychologist practice typically requires a doctoral degree, supervised experience, examination and state licensure; other psychology careers have different requirements.
Career Launch
Work in clinical, school, research, organizational or community settings depending on degree/credential path.
Psychologist.scene: a calm professional psychology office or research setting, dressed in professional attire, meeting respectfully with a client or reviewing behavioral research materials, no visible private patient information

Architect: Often 7–10+ years from high school to independent licensure, depending on degree and experience route.
Electrician: Often about 4–5 years in a paid apprenticeship/training route, with licensing requirements varying by state.
Registered Nurse: Commonly 2–4 years after high school for an ADN/BSN route, followed by NCLEX-RN licensure.
Veterinarian: Usually about 8 years after high school before entering practice: undergraduate preparation plus a 4-year DVM program.
Software Developer: Often 2–4+ years after high school depending on degree, community-college, certificate or portfolio-based route.
Teacher: Usually 4+ years after high school for a bachelor’s degree and educator preparation, plus state certification requirements.
Special Education Teacher: Usually 4+ years after high school for a degree and special-education teacher preparation, plus state certification requirements.
Firefighter: Can range from months to several years after high school depending on hiring cycles, academy and EMT requirements.
Police Officer: Often 1–4+ years after high school depending on college choices, minimum-age rules and agency hiring/academy requirements.
TV News Reporter / Local Anchor: Often 4 years for a journalism/communications degree, though portfolio and internship strength are major hiring factors.
Broadway Director / Actor: Highly variable; formal BFA/BA training is often 4 years, but professional progress depends on auditions, credits and network.
Chef / Restaurant Owner: Can begin directly after high school; culinary programs often run 1–4 years, while ownership usually follows substantial industry experience.
Automotive Technician: Commonly 1–2 years of postsecondary technical study or employer training, followed by continued ASE/manufacturer certification.
Physical Therapist: Usually about 7 years after high school: undergraduate preparation plus a 3-year DPT program.
Plumber: Often about 4–5 years in apprenticeship before full journeyperson-level qualification, depending on state rules.
Business Administration / Manager: Often 4 years for a bachelor’s degree; some entry paths begin sooner through work experience or associate-degree programs.
Carpenter: Can begin directly after high school; apprenticeship commonly takes 3–4 years to reach advanced journeyperson skill.
Graphic Designer: Often 2–4 years of design study, though portfolio-based entry routes also exist.
Neurosurgeon: Commonly 15+ years after high school: college, medical school and about 7 years of neurosurgery residency, sometimes followed by fellowship.
Cybersecurity Specialist: Often 2–4 years of college/training, though certification + experience routes can begin sooner.
Data Scientist / AI Specialist: Often 4 years for entry-level data/AI roles; advanced research positions may require graduate study.
Dental Hygienist: Often 2–3 years after high school for an associate-level dental-hygiene program, plus licensing exams.
Doctor / Physician: Usually 11–15+ years after high school depending on specialty: college, medical school and residency/fellowship.
HVAC Technician: Often 1–2 years of technical education plus employer/apprenticeship experience; advancement continues through field hours and certifications.
Lawyer / Attorney: Usually about 7 years after high school: 4-year bachelor’s degree + 3-year JD, followed by bar admission.
Marketing / Advertising Professional: Often 4 years for a bachelor’s degree, though portfolio/internship-based entry paths can begin sooner.
Medical & Health Services Manager: Often 4 years for a bachelor’s degree; management advancement may take additional experience or graduate study.
Nurse Practitioner: Often 6–8+ years after high school depending on BSN/RN experience and MSN/DNP pathway.
Occupational Therapist: Usually 6–7 years after high school: bachelor’s preparation plus an OT master’s/doctoral professional program.
Physician Assistant: Often 6–7 years after high school: bachelor’s/prerequisites + patient-care experience + roughly 2–3 years of PA school.
School Counselor / Mental Health Counsel: Usually 6+ years after high school: bachelor’s degree plus a counseling master’s and supervised credentialing requirements.
Web / Digital Designer: Often 2–4 years of college/training, though portfolio-based entry routes can be faster.
Welder / Fabricator: Often 6 months–2 years of technical training, followed by continuing skill/certification development on the job.
Engineer: Typically 4 years for a bachelor’s degree; professional licensure, when pursued, requires additional exams/experience.
Accountant / Financial Manager: Often 4 years for a bachelor’s degree; CPA or advanced finance credentials can add time/experience requirements.
Entrepreneur / Business Owner: Can begin in high school or immediately after; success depends more on execution, market fit and financial discipline than a fixed timeline.
Military / Armed Forces: Varies widely by route: enlistment can begin after high school; officer paths commonly include a 4-year college/academy route before commissioning.
Customer Service Representative: Can begin directly after high school; advancement depends strongly on communication, reliability and industry knowledge.
Elected Official / Politician: No fixed timeline; some people run for local office soon after becoming eligible, while others build careers/community records first.
Caregiver / Personal Care Aide: Can begin soon after high school; formal caregiver/CNA/HHA training often takes weeks to months depending on role.
Construction Manager: Often 4 years for a construction-management degree, with internships/co-ops building the field experience employers expect.
Psychologist: About 4 years for bachelor-level psychology roles; licensed clinical psychologist pathways commonly take 8–12+ years after high school.
